A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LatentChem study and contain readable main text and appendices A–Q. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish correspondence of the figures, tables, equations, and appendix material without material gaps.

before.justification: v5 reports original model evaluations on four chemical benchmarks, component ablations, latent-budget and noise-intervention experiments, and latency measurements.

after.justification: v6 retains these original benchmark evaluations and experimental analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The architecture, latent-thinking loop, training stages, and objectives are unchanged. Appendix C's correction from four reward terms to three matches the three components already specified in v5's Section 3.3 and Appendix D.4; no reward component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions train on ChemCoTDataset and evaluate the same task coverage from ChemCoTBench, Mol-Instructions, ChEBI-20, and ChemLLMBench. No evaluated dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same text-only Qwen models, explicit chemical LLM stages, and Coconut-Chem baseline. The additional comparisons and training variants in Appendices J and M are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Evaluation samples, metrics, model scales, training budgets, and testing procedures remain unchanged, including the latency protocol in Appendix K and overlap protocol in Appendix P. No experiment introduces a new or revised setting.

E4.justification: The component ablations, Gaussian-noise interventions, budget stress tests, latent-representation analyses, and appendix diagnostics are retained unchanged. This includes the topology-sensitive and counterfactual-alignment ablations in Appendices N and O.

E5.justification: Both retain the sign-test significance reporting in Table 3, standard-error bars in Figure 5, and repeated evaluations across seeds 2026–2075 with mean and standard deviation in Appendix Q.

E6.justification: Reported numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged, including the 59.88% ChemCoTBench non-tie win rate and reported efficiency results. The introductory sentence about reductions exceeding 28× is removed, but the corresponding 28.4× optimization and 29.9× reaction results remain in Figure 8 and Table 16.

T1.justification: Appendix A's definitions, assumptions, Theorem A.9, proof, and efficiency-scaling analysis are unchanged. The method equations and training-loss formulations are also retained.

C1.justification: The abstract changes from claiming empirical evidence for the latent-space hypothesis to saying the results are consistent with it. The introduction also qualifies the performance contribution as 'overall' superior, modestly narrowing the retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 adds that absolute reaction-prediction accuracy remains modest, qualifying its discussion of competitive performance using the unchanged results in Tables 6 and 7. The broader mechanism explanations and existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C corrects the documented reward-component count from four to three, resolving an inconsistency with its existing list and Appendix D.4. This is a documentation correction; hyperparameters, hardware, and code/model access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to explicit CoT and generic latent reasoning are unchanged. The new ICML proceedings notice is publication metadata rather than revised research positioning.

P1.justification: There are localized sentence edits in the abstract, introduction, and results discussion, a reward-count correction, and updated publication text. The section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Local reflow adjusts spacing and Table 5's position. On page 9, the conclusion heading moves from the bottom of the left column to accompany its opening paragraph in the right column. Figures and table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: v6 modestly improves scientific calibration through the more cautious abstract and the explicit reaction-accuracy limitation, supported by the low absolute accuracies already reported in Tables 6 and 7. The reward-count correction and conclusion-heading placement also improve consistency and readability. The underlying evidence and most substantive argumentation remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
